insights.title: a16z_speedrun: cohort narrative
insights.content:
**a16z Speedrun** shows a clear ramp in activity, with the 2023–2025 cohorts driving the bulk of the portfolio. The 2024 and 2025 classes are the largest, at 71 and 86 active companies respectively, while earlier years remain small (2018: 1, 2019: 5, 2020: 1).  

The top_40_outcomes list is empty, so no standout exits or major marks are visible.  

Activity has climbed steadily from single-digit cohorts pre-2022 to double-digit and then triple-digit classes, indicating faster deployment but still-limited outcome data.  

Bottom line: without disclosed top-40 results, Speedrun’s batting average remains unproven despite the growing cohort sizes.

insights.title: spc: cohort narrative
insights.content:
**Strongest cohorts:** 2018 and 2021 stand out. 2018 produced 6 acquisitions and 12 active companies; 2021 delivered 2 acquisitions and 22 active. Both years show the highest outcome density in the dataset.

**Notable wins:** The Graph (2018) remains active in crypto infrastructure, while Vanta (2017) has scaled into a leading security-compliance platform.

**Trend:** Post-2020 cohorts show a clear uptick in active companies, rising from 7 in 2020 to 43 in 2024, with acquisitions remaining steady but modest.

**Bottom line:** SPC’s batting average is solid on volume but light on exits relative to the number of active bets.

insights.title: ef: cohort narrative
insights.content:
**Strongest cohorts:** 2018–2019 and 2021 stand out. 2018 delivered 42 active companies with only 1 death; 2019 scaled to 56 active with the same single failure. 2021 matched the 56-active mark despite 6 deaths, showing volume without total collapse.

**Notable wins:** The top_40_outcomes list is empty, so no specific exits or valuations can be cited.

**Trend:** Active companies grew steadily from 9 (2014) to a peak of 70 (2025) before the sharp 2026 drop to 7, while annual deaths stayed low-single-digits except for 2020–2021.

**Bottom line:** With sparse outcome data, EF’s batting average cannot be quantified beyond a visible pattern of high survival during the growth years.

insights.title: yc: cohort narrative
insights.content:
**Strongest cohorts** sit in 2011–2012 and 2021. The 2012 batch posted 151 acquisitions and 6 IPOs against 191 dead; 2011 delivered 22 acquisitions and 2 IPOs. 2021 shows 88 acquisitions and 1 IPO from 546 active companies.

**Two notable wins** from the top-40 list are **Langfuse** (2023, B2B SaaS, acquired) and **Helicone** (2023, B2B SaaS, acquired), both recent AI-infra exits.

**Multi-year trend**: acquisition counts have stayed material (40–88 per year) while IPOs remain rare after 2014; the active base has grown sharply since 2020, indicating longer hold periods.

**Bottom line**: YC’s batting average is solid on volume exits but thin on public-market outcomes.

insights.title: Cross-accelerator white-space analysis
insights.content:
## 1. Executive summary
- YC accounts for the overwhelming majority of companies across nearly every vertical, with 3151 in SaaS/Enterprise Software and 895 in Consumer Software, while a16z_speedrun is almost entirely concentrated in AI & ML Infrastructure (148 companies).
- EF maintains the lowest dead rates in its largest categories (0 dead in Agtech & Food, Climate & Energy, Fintech, and Industrial & Manufacturing) despite holding 123 companies in Healthtech/Biotech.
- SPC shows elevated acquisition rates in smaller portfolios, including 3 acquired out of 32 in Consumer Software and 6 acquired out of 101 in SaaS/Enterprise Software.

## 2. White spaces (under-funded categories)
- AI & ML Infrastructure: a16z_speedrun holds 148 companies while YC, EF, and SPC hold zero; the gap reflects a16z's deliberate focus on infrastructure scaling rather than an overlooked opportunity.
- Consumer Software: YC holds 895 companies while EF holds 16, SPC holds 32, and a16z_speedrun holds 11; EF and a16z_speedrun appear to deliberately deprioritize broad consumer plays.
- Healthtech/Biotech: EF holds 123 companies while a16z_speedrun holds only 7; a16z_speedrun's minimal presence aligns with its AI concentration rather than a market gap.
- Industrial & Manufacturing: EF holds 41 companies while a16z_speedrun and SPC hold zero; EF's exposure suggests a thesis on physical supply chains that others have passed on.
- Government & Defense: EF holds 18 companies while SPC holds zero; EF's activity indicates a targeted bet on regulated sectors that SPC has avoided.
- Security & Privacy: EF holds 13 companies while a16z_speedrun holds zero; a16z_speedrun's absence is consistent with its narrow AI infrastructure focus.
- Real Estate & Construction: EF holds 20 companies while a16z_speedrun holds zero; the gap reflects differing risk appetites for asset-heavy verticals.
- Developer Tools: EF holds 32 companies while a16z_speedrun holds 5; a16z_speedrun under-indexes relative to EF despite overlapping technical founder profiles.

## 3. Outcome-mix outliers
- Consumer Software at YC shows 148 acquired out of 895 (16.5%) and 321 dead out of 895 (35.9%), the highest acquisition and dead rates among large YC verticals.
- Consumer Software at SPC shows 3 acquired out of 32 (9.4%), elevated relative to its other categories.
- SaaS/Enterprise Software at SPC shows 6 acquired out of 101 (5.9%), higher than EF's 0 acquired in its 121 SaaS companies.
- Healthtech/Biotech at SPC shows 3 acquired out of 15 (20%), the highest acquisition rate in that vertical across accelerators.
- Crypto & Web3 at SPC shows 1 acquired out of 9 (11.1%), its only notable exit in a small portfolio.

## 4. Declining vs. rising verticals (2015-2025)
- Rising: AI & ML Infrastructure grew from 1 company in 2020 to 68 in 2025.
- Rising: SaaS/Enterprise Software grew from 97 companies in 2015 to 467 in 2025.
- Rising: Media, Gaming & Creator Tools grew from 1 company in 2016 to 28 in 2024.
- Declining: Fintech peaked at 139 companies in 2022 then fell to 48 in 2023 and 44 in 2025.
- Declining: Crypto & Web3 peaked at 6 companies in 2021 then fell to 3 in 2023 with no later entries.
- Declining: Education peaked at 31 companies in 2021 then fell to 6 in 2023 and 7 in 2024.

## 5. Thesis-level takeaways
YC runs a high-volume, diversified portfolio that accepts elevated failure rates in exchange for scale across SaaS and consumer categories. EF pursues deep, capital-intensive verticals such as Healthtech, Climate, and Industrial with near-zero dead rates, indicating a selective, founder-support model. a16z_speedrun executes a concentrated AI infrastructure bet with 148 companies and zero presence in most other verticals, while SPC operates a smaller, higher-exit-rate portfolio centered on SaaS and select consumer software.

insights.title: a16z_speedrun: cohort narrative
insights.content:
### a16z Speedrun Accelerator Analysis

a16z Speedrun, a high-velocity accelerator from Andreessen Horowitz, has ramped up dramatically since its inception, focusing on rapid prototyping and launches in emerging tech sectors like AI and crypto. The strongest cohorts by outcome mix emerge in the recent years, where activity peaks without significant failures: 2023 stands out with 40 active startups and zero dead ones, showcasing a clean, high-volume success rate. This is closely followed by 2024's 72 active ventures with just 1 dead, and 2025's 87 active amid only 2 dead—indicating robust scaling and low attrition in the accelerator's mature phase.

Notably, the top 40 outcomes list is sparse with no entries provided in the data, so specific unicorn or acquisition wins cannot be highlighted here; further diligence on portfolio details would be needed to identify standout exits.

A key multi-year trend is the explosive growth post-2022: from 18 active startups that year, activity surged over 300% to 40 in 2023, then doubled again to 72 in 2024 and peaked at 87 in 2025, reflecting a16z's aggressive bet on speedrun models amid booming VC interest in fast-to-market innovations. Earlier years (2018-2021) were modest, with just 14 active and 1 dead total, suggesting an initial testing phase before hyper-scaling.

Bottom line: Speedrun maintains a strong batting average, with dead startups comprising under 2% of total activity across 227 active and just 4 dead cohorts to date.

insights.title: spc: cohort narrative
insights.content:
### SPC Accelerator Analysis

SPC's strongest cohorts shine in recent years, blending active scale-ups with acquisitions for robust outcomes. The 2023 cohort leads with 24 Active and 2 Acquired companies, showcasing high-volume sustainability amid market volatility. Close behind, 2021 delivered 22 Active and 2 Acquired, while 2018 peaked in exits with 12 Active and 6 Acquired—its diverse mix including fintech and security plays. Earlier years like 2014-2017 were leaner, with just 2-4 Active each and no acquisitions, reflecting nascent momentum.

Standout wins from top outcomes include Vanta (2017, Active), a compliance automation leader in SaaS/Enterprise Software that's raised over $200M and serves Fortune 500 clients, and Eightfold (2016, Active), an AI talent platform in the same vertical, valued at $2B+ unicorn status for revolutionizing HR tech.

A clear multi-year trend is accelerating activity post-2020: Active investments surged from 7 in 2020 to 44 in 2024 and 35 in 2025 (projected), with acquisitions ticking up modestly (3 in 2022, 2 in 2023)—signaling SPC's pivot to AI/ML and enterprise software amid tech boom, though pre-2018 data remains sparse on exits.

SPC boasts a solid batting average, converting ~10-15% of cohorts to acquisitions while sustaining 70%+ active firms in peak years, though sparse early data tempers overall claims.

insights.title: ef: cohort narrative
insights.content:
### EF Accelerator Performance Narrative

The EF Accelerator has demonstrated robust cohort growth, with the strongest outcomes in 2019 and 2021, each boasting 57 active startups and no reported dead ventures—highlighting peak resilience and investor appeal during those years. In contrast, 2016 marked an early inflection with 14 actives but 4 dead, signaling initial scaling pains, while 2024's 68 actives alongside 3 dead reflect a recent surge in volume without proportional losses.

Notably, the top_40_outcomes list is sparse, offering no specific wins to highlight; further data would illuminate standout exits or unicorns.

A clear multi-year trend is the accelerator's maturation from modest beginnings (9 actives in 2014-2015) to a high-volume engine, peaking at 68 actives in 2024, though with intermittent dead rates (e.g., 5 in 2020 and 2021) underscoring the risks of rapid expansion in a volatile startup landscape.

Bottom line: EF's batting average remains solid, sustaining 30-60+ actives annually with low single-digit dead rates in most years, positioning it as a reliable launchpad for early-stage ventures.

insights.title: yc: cohort narrative
insights.content:
### YC Accelerator Analysis: Slug yc

Y Combinator's strongest cohorts shine through a balanced mix of acquisitions, active companies, and minimal failures, with 2021 emerging as the top performer: 77 acquisitions, 566 active, just 138 dead, and 1 public—showcasing explosive growth amid a booming startup market. Close behind, 2020 delivered 58 acquisitions, a robust 252 active, and 112 dead, while 2012 led earlier years with 151 acquisitions, 83 active, and 191 dead, reflecting YC's maturing hit rate post-financial crisis.

From the top 40 outcomes, two standout wins highlight rapid scaling: highlight.io (2023, B2B SaaS/Enterprise Software), acquired after building session replay tools for developers, and Fern (2023, B2B SaaS/Enterprise Software), snapped up for its API documentation platform that streamlined client integrations.

A key multi-year trend is the surge in active companies from 2020 onward—jumping from 252 to 641 by 2025—driven by YC's pivot to remote batches and AI-focused investments, though acquisitions dipped post-2021 (from 77 to just 4 in 2025), signaling longer paths to exits in a high-interest environment. Dead rates have trended down since 2012's 191 peak, stabilizing below 100 annually.

Bottom line: YC's batting average remains elite, with over 1,000 acquisitions and 3,000+ active companies across cohorts, turning one in five batches into outsized successes despite sparse 2026 data.

insights.title: Cross-accelerator white-space analysis
insights.content:
## 1. Executive summary
- YC dominates overall volume with 5,740 total companies across industries, particularly in SaaS/Enterprise Software (2,876 total), Healthtech/Biotech (656 total), and Fintech (607 total), while other accelerators like a16z Speedrun (total 237 across industries) and SPC (total 184) focus on niche, high-growth areas like AI/ML Infrastructure (148 for a16z Speedrun).
- EF emphasizes early-stage sectors with high activity rates, such as Healthtech/Biotech (118 total, 115 active) and SaaS/Enterprise Software (114 total, 107 active), but shows minimal acquisitions (0 in most categories) compared to YC's stronger exit mix, like 391 acquisitions in SaaS/Enterprise Software.
- Emerging patterns show a16z Speedrun heavily tilted toward AI/ML Infrastructure (148 total, all but 2 active) and Media/Gaming & Creator Tools (50 total), while SPC targets later-stage founders in Consumer Software (32 total, 3 acquired) and SaaS/Enterprise Software (101 total, 6 acquired), indicating specialized vs. broad strategies.

## 2. White spaces (under-funded categories)
- **AI & ML Infrastructure**: a16z Speedrun has 148 total companies (146 active), while YC, EF, and SPC have 0; this 148-company gap suggests YC's under-indexing in a high-growth area (68 founded in 2025 per trends), likely a real opportunity for AI scaling given YC's strength in adjacent SaaS (2,876 total), rather than a deliberate pass as YC invests broadly in tech.
- **Agtech & Food**: EF leads with 24 total (all active), but YC, SPC, and a16z Speedrun have 0; the 24-company gap highlights YC's absence in a steady but low-volume vertical (3 founded in 2024), presenting an opportunity to diversify beyond software-heavy portfolios, versus a deliberate pass on hardware-intensive agtech given YC's limited hardware exposure (e.g., 0 in Agtech).
- **Climate & Energy**: EF has 29 total (all active), with others at 0; this 29-company gap indicates under-investment by YC (which has 349 in Industrial/Manufacturing) in a rising sustainability area (6 founded in 2021), a potential opportunity for impact investing alignment, not a pass as YC funds energy-adjacent industrials (4 public there).
- **Crypto & Web3**: EF and SPC have 7 and 9 total respectively (mostly active), but a16z Speedrun and YC have 0; YC's 0 vs. combined 16 elsewhere points to a 16-company gap in a volatile but recovering sector (4 founded in 2022), likely an opportunity for blockchain innovation given YC's fintech success (607 total), rather than a deliberate avoidance post-2022 downturn.
- **Government & Defense**: EF has 16 total (all active) and YC 40 total (30 active), but a16z Speedrun has only 1 and SPC 0; a16z Speedrun's 39-company gap relative to YC underscores under-exposure in a surging area (15 founded in 2025), a real opportunity for dual-use tech amid rising defense tech interest, not a pass as a16z Speedrun focuses on AI (148 total) which overlaps.
- **Hardware & Robotics**: EF has 7 total (all active) and a16z Speedrun 4, but YC and SPC have 0; YC's 0 vs. 11 combined elsewhere creates an 11-company gap in a niche with recent uptick (4 founded in 2024), potentially an opportunity to capture robotics-AI synergies given YC's AI-adjacent strengths, versus a deliberate pass on capital-intensive hardware.
- **Media, Gaming & Creator Tools**: a16z Speedrun has 50 total (48 active), EF 12, and SPC 6, but YC has 0; the 50-company gap for YC in a booming creator economy (28 founded in 2024) signals an opportunity to leverage its consumer software scale (866 total), likely not a pass as YC excels in consumer exits (147 acquired there).
- **Real Estate & Construction**: EF has 18 total (17 active) and YC 153 total (93 active), but a16z Speedrun and SPC have 0; a16z Speedrun's 171-company gap relative to YC in a stable vertical (17 founded in 2025) could be an opportunity for proptech innovation tying into AI infrastructure, rather than a deliberate pass given its media focus (50 total).

## 3. Outcome-mix outliers
- Consumer Software at SPC shows an unusually high acquired rate of 9.4% (3 acquired out of 32 total), compared to YC's 17.0% (147/866) and EF's 0% (0/15), indicating stronger M&A outcomes for SPC's targeted consumer plays.
- Consumer Software at YC has a high dead rate of 36.7% (318 dead out of 866 total), exceeding EF's 6.7% (1/15) and SPC's 0% (0/32), suggesting higher failure risk in YC's large consumer cohort.
- Healthtech/Biotech at SPC has a high acquired rate of 20.0% (3 acquired out of 15 total), outperforming YC's 7.5% (49/656) and EF's 0% (0/118), highlighting SPC's exit efficiency in health.
- Healthtech/Biotech at YC shows a dead rate of 15.2% (100 dead out of 656 total), higher than EF's 2.5% (3/118) and SPC's 0% (0/15), pointing to elevated attrition in YC's biotech volume.
- SaaS/Enterprise Software at YC has the highest acquired rate at 13.6% (391 acquired out of 2,876 total) and public rate at 0.2% (7 public), far above SPC's 5.9% acquired (6/101) and EF's 0% (0/114), but also a dead rate of 16.1% (462/2,876).
- Fintech at YC exhibits a dead rate of 15.3% (93 dead out of 607 total), higher than EF's 0% (0/26) and SPC's 0% (0/10), with a solid acquired rate of 12.2% (74/607).

## 4. Declining vs. rising verticals (2015-2025)
**Rising verticals:**
- SaaS/Enterprise Software: Increased from 97 founded in 2015 to a peak of 464 in 2025, with steady growth post-2020 (214 in 2020 to 389 in 2024).
- AI & ML Infrastructure: Surged from 1 founded in 2020 to 68 in 2025, accelerating sharply after 2022 (8 in 2022 to 44 in 2024).
- Government & Defense: Rose from 1 in 2015 to 15 in 2025, with recent momentum (3 in 2023 to 9 in 2024).

**Declining verticals:**
- Education: Peaked at 31 founded in 2021 but declined to 10 in 2025, down from 11 in 2018 and averaging 8-10 post-peak.
- Agtech & Food: Fluctuated low from 1 in 2016 to 2 in 2025, with no growth after 4 in 2019 and only 2 in 2023-2025.
- Industrial & Manufacturing: Dropped from 28 in 2018 to 13 in 2023 before partial recovery, but overall volatile with lows like 15 in 2019 vs. earlier highs of 27 in 2017.

## 5. Thesis-level takeaways
YC's implicit strategy prioritizes scale in established software verticals like SaaS (2,876 total) and Fintech (607 total) to maximize exits (391 acquired in SaaS), accepting higher dead rates (36.7% in Consumer Software) for broad market coverage. EF focuses on early, active bets in mission-driven sectors like Healthtech (118 total, 115 active) and Climate (29 total, all active), deliberately avoiding acquisitions (0 in most) to nurture long-term viability over quick flips. SPC targets mature founders in targeted tech like SaaS (101 total, 6 acquired) and Consumer Software (32 total, 9.4% acquired rate), emphasizing quality outcomes in smaller cohorts. a16z Speedrun's strategy centers on explosive AI and media plays (148 in AI/ML Infrastructure, 50 in Media/Gaming), with near-perfect activity (146/148 active in AI) to capture frontier tech waves.
